subject: PrivDeploy support uplift & incident-credit structure proposal
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@synthex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PrivDeploy support uplift & incident-credit structure proposal

Alex — thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, attached is a tailored support proposal for Synthex's VPC deployment that addresses the two procurement concerns you raised: predictable OPEX treatment and protection against early-stage reliability risk during go-live. High level: 

- Pilot credits: 6 months of platform-fee credits (up to $75k) applied to the first invoice if you sign the SOW before Sept 30.
- Incident-credit ladder: credits tied to uptime + timeto-restore (RTO) breaches — defined tiered offsets rather than ad-hoc credits. This is intended to make remediation economics predictable for your finance team.
- Support uplift options: Standard / Enhanced / Critical — Enhanced includes a 2x faster triage SLA and named escalation engineer; Critical includes weekend on-call and quarterly runbook reviews.
- Operator vs site license note: we recommend an operator license for your multi-cluster pilot to reduce up-front seat counting; pricing shown in attachment.

I attached: PrivDeploy_Tiered_Support_Proposal.pdf and a draft SOW (SOW-draft.docx). I think the combination of pilot credits + the incident-credit ladder will satisfy your procurement team’s call for defined remedies while keeping platform fee capitalization optional.

Next steps: if this shape looks ok I can route a redlined SOW and a DocuSign envelope for an initial pilot commitment; Marissa has offered to coordinate an ops readiness call next week to lock the runbook expectations.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0196

Attachments: PrivDeploy_Tiered_Support_Proposal.pdf (PDF, 6 pages), SOW-draft.docx (DOCX, 12 pages)

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@synthex.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Synthex Procurement <procurement@synthex.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy support uplift & incident-credit structure proposal

Irene — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear framing. A few immediate questions from my side and I'll route to procurement: 

1) The pilot credit language: is the $75k a hard cap per SOW or per account? We need it to be caps-per-legal-entity for accounting.
2) Incident-credit ladder: can you convert the ladder into a fixed percent-of-platform-fee refund schedule (i.e., 5% / 10% / 25%) so our controllers can model worst-case?
3) Operator license: procurement will push back on anything that looks like an unlimited seat exposure. Can you provide how operator licensing is metered, or a swap to a site license with a 90-day true-up?

Also — we have an internal deadline: procurement must have final commercial terms for our Q4 budget review by Aug 26. Can you confirm if Redwood can commit to an Aug 26 sign-off timeline if we move quickly?

Thanks,
Alex
CTO, Synthex Health
alex.morgan@synthex.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@synthex.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 12:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy support uplift & incident-credit structure proposal

Looping in a couple of product-pricing clarifications that should help with procurement modeling (quick bullets):

- Pilot credit scope: we can confirm $75k cap is per legal-entity. We'll reflect that in the SOW note.
- Refund-as-percent: happy to convert the ladder to the fixed-percent model. Proposed mapping (draft): Severity 1 breach => 25% platform-fee credit; Severity 2 => 10%; Severity 3 => 3%. We'll bake caps by month so exposure is bounded.
- Operator metering: suggest a hybrid: operator license for pilot (counts named operators only) + 90-day true-up to site licenses on production go-live. That gives Synthex predictable pilot costs and addresses seat exposure.

Irene — I attached a one-pager in the proposal showing the percent-based mapping and monthly cap examples. If Alex is comfortable with the percent mapping and the per-entity cap, I recommend we issue a revised SOW by Monday and prepare a DocuSign envelope to meet their Aug 26 procurement window.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy support uplift & incident-credit structure proposal

Alex — quick note from an SRE / packaging perspective: if you take the hybrid operator -> site true-up model, we can include a 30-day notification window and a capped true-up fee that doesn't exceed the published 12-month operator-to-site conversion delta. That typically smooths procurement risk and keeps accounting clean.

Irene/Marissa — if we keep the pilot credit as-is and adopt the percent-based incident credits, we should also add a limitation clause for third-party-caused incidents (e.g., network provider outages) so credits are only Redwood-responsibility tied. I'll draft the exact wording for SOW.

-Ben

ben_carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: PrivDeploy support uplift & incident-credit structure proposal

Team — thanks for the clarifications. Procurement reviewed the attachments and wants two final adjustments before they can sign: 

1) Convert the incident-credit ladder to the fixed-percent mapping Marissa proposed and show a 6-month worst-case exposure example.
2) Add specific carveouts for third-party network outages, maintenance windows, and customer-induced configuration errors.

If you can provide a redlined SOW with those two changes by EOD Thursday (Aug 20) we'll see if procurement can turn it around for our Aug 26 budget review. Also please include a short summary (one paragraph) for our CFO explaining why the pilot credit is structured as a pre-production offset rather than an up-front rebate (they want the accounting rationale).

I'll wait for the redline.

-Alex
CTO, Synthex Health
